title: Puducherry to Give Rs 700 Diwali Hampers to Three Lakh Ration Card Families
excerpt: Each free hamper carries sugar, sunflower oil, chana dal, rava and maida, distributed through fair price shops before the festival, Minister V. P. Sivakolundhu announced in Karaikal.
body:
• The Puducherry government will give a free Diwali gift hamper worth Rs 700 to three lakh ration cardholder families across the Union Territory — a total outlay of about Rs 21 crore.
  • Each hamper contains five grocery essentials: 2 kg sugar, 2 litres of sunflower oil, 1 kg chana dal, 500 g rava and 500 g maida.
  • Distribution will run through all fair price shops before the festival, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister V. P. Sivakolundhu announced in Karaikal.
  • Families should collect from their usual fair price shop ahead of Diwali; the government has directed outlets to ensure smooth, timely distribution.

The Puducherry government will distribute a Diwali gift hamper worth Rs 700, free of cost, to three lakh ration cardholder families across the Union Territory, the Times of India reported. Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister V. P. Sivakolundhu announced the scheme during a visit to Karaikal on Tuesday.

What Is in the Hamper

Each hamper carries five essential grocery items chosen for festival cooking: 2 kg of sugar, 2 litres of sunflower oil, 1 kg of chana dal, 500 g of rava and 500 g of maida. At Rs 700 per family across three lakh families, the programme amounts to roughly Rs 21 crore of groceries moving through the territory's public distribution system in the run-up to Diwali.

"The Puducherry government will distribute a Diwali gift hamper worth Rs 700, free of cost, to three lakh ration cardholder families across the Union Territory, the Times of India reported."

How Distribution Will Work

The hampers will be distributed through all fair price shops in the Union Territory, and the government has instructed every outlet to ensure smooth and timely distribution so families can celebrate the festival without financial strain. Ration cardholders collect from the fair price shop they normally use — the same channel the territory has used for earlier festival distributions of rice and sugar through the PDS.

Why It Matters Beyond Puducherry

Festival hampers are a recurring feature of welfare politics in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, where Pongal and Diwali packages reach effectively every ration cardholder household rather than a narrow beneficiary list. For the large Puducherry-origin diaspora — concentrated in France and the Gulf as well as across India — the practical relevance is at the family end: parents and relatives on ration cards in Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam will receive the hamper automatically through their shop, with no application step for families abroad to manage on their behalf.

The announcement lands in a busy festival-spending season in the territory. Distribution is scheduled to be completed before Diwali, and cardholders who find their local shop out of stock in the first round should expect the directed restocking the minister's announcement promised.
